decisions.reason: As an organic extension of the firm's established ham and sliced deli expertise, it fits existing knowledge, certified systems and strategic expansion of organic lines, so the firm is likely to retain it and refine it rather than exit quickly.

Organic sliced cured smoked pork is very close to the firm's core processing capabilities and customer base, which gives management enough related knowledge to learn from early sales and improve the offer.

An organic pepper-coated salami builds directly on the firm's salami know-how and seasoning capabilities, making it a plausible product to keep while leveraging absorptive capacity in organic and cured meats.

This exotic teriyaki aspic specialty is more niche and less aligned with the firm's traditional premium meat positioning, so despite aspic competence the firm is more likely to redeploy resources if early traction was limited.

Fennel-flavoured sliced salami still sits within the firm's core salami category and seasoning expertise, but its more distinctive taste profile makes it somewhat riskier and more dependent on proving repeat demand.

A liver pâté with veal closely matches the firm's pâté capabilities, premium positioning and deli channels, so management would likely see enough scope to adapt and commercialize it rather than discontinue it soon.
